Source body mapping: Held at: below the heart. Felt in the lower sternum.
conflicts: The record combines a project-defined affect label with a specific bodily location; this does not establish anatomical causation.

researchPasses.name: independent_affect_science_review
findings: Anticipation involves prediction and affective preparation; it is not a discrete emotion with an established lower-sternum storage site.
Meta-analytic emotion research finds little evidence that discrete emotions can be consistently localized to unique brain regions; interacting networks contribute across categories.
conflicts: Project-specific labels such as Apathy and Shock do not necessarily correspond to a universally agreed basic-emotion taxonomy.

researchPasses.name: adversarial_localization_and_counterexample_review
findings: Counterexample: the same bodily sensation can accompany different emotional states, medical conditions, movement, or context; the sensation does not identify the emotion.
The record remains usable as a symbolic map only; no clinical or anatomical inference is allowed.
conflicts: The body-location assignment remains an owner-model hypothesis, not an empirically validated mechanism.
